feed.title: NPR Topics: News
feed.subtitle: NPR news, audio, and podcasts. Coverage of breaking stories, national and world news, politics, business, science, technology, and extended coverage of major national and world events.

entry.title: Gut microbes followed migrating humans across continents, new study suggests
entry.summary: New research looks at the surprising similarities in the gut microbiomes of hunter-gathers in Tanzania and horticulturalists in Bolivia, and asks: What role do these bacteria play in human health?

entry.title: Greetings from Lahore, Pakistan, whose high court offers an oasis for chatter and chai
entry.summary: The Lahore High Court is a near-perfect specimen of British South Asian colonial architecture and its main square is a pleasant spot shaded by banyan trees.

entry.title: DIY fertilizer is a blessing as farmers face steep prices due to the Iran war
entry.summary: It's hard enough being a small-scale farmer. Then the Iran war drove up fertilizer prices. So farmers are using a traditional Asian recipe to make their own. They call it a "labor of love."

entry.title: U.S. moves long-range bombers from U.K. And, Israel allegedly warned before Oct. 7
entry.summary: A possible Iranian threat led the U.S. to remove long-range bombers from a U.K. base. And, Israelis are learning that their prime minister may have been warned before the Oct. 7 attacks.

entry.title: Who will win the 2026 Nobel Prize in economics?
entry.summary: A thinly traded prediction market offers a starting point. We explore potential winners and the big ideas that could earn them economics' biggest prize.

entry.title: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai win Nobel Prize in chemistry
entry.summary: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai won the Nobel Prize in chemistry Wednesday for their discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis.

entry.title: BTS frontman RM is showing his art collection. Fans are flocking to see it
entry.summary: The pop superstar is showing art from his personal collection for the first time. The San Francisco Museum of Modern Art is packed with fans.

entry.title: Over 1,000 children are buried at juvenile detention centers nationwide
entry.summary: Researchers uncovered the graves of more than 1,000 children next to juvenile detention facilities in 29 states. At one Maryland gravesite, 230 Black boys are buried.

entry.title: An early flu season means it might be time to think about a flu shot
entry.summary: Flu season typically starts in October or November. But it looks like the flu started to pick up in September this year.

entry.title: 'Medicare for All' message attracts midterm voters buckling under medical bills
entry.summary: Midterm candidates are talking up Medicare for All, and in a poll 2 out of 3 Americans said they support it. The phrase speaks to a desire for radical change, though many don't really know what it is.
